definition.en: The stem of a plant, the part from the base up to the first branch. The word also means a tree or a pole.

notes: To count as muhi, a stem must have a base (sina or kolo), so underground stems such as tubers and rhizomes are not mihi. Mgombato glosses muhi as 'non-cultivated plant, tree'.

definition.en: The base of the trunk, just above the ground.

meaning.en: Used of people for an ancestor or a person's place of birth.

notes: Kolo means the same.

definition.en: Another word for sina, the base of the trunk just above the ground.

meaning.en: Used of people for ancestry or historical links.

notes: Mgombato glosses kolo more broadly, as 'stem, tree trunk'.

definition.en: The bark of a tree.

meaning.en: Also the scab or cover over a wound. Pakia argues the Digo treat bark and skin as matching structures.

definition.en: An injury or scar on the bark of a tree.

meaning.en: Wound, sore.

notes: Pakia suggests the word passed from people to plants after gopha (wound cover) was used for bark.

definition.en: A ring cut by stripping the bark all the way round a stem, which kills the plant. Doing this is kupiga chilingo.
Growths on bark, such as lichens.

meaning.en: Hair; probably borrowed from Swahili nywele.

definition.en: The wood inside a tree trunk.

meaning.en: 'Meat of a tree': the grain looks like chunks of meat, and nyama is the inner substance of any living thing.

notes: Coconut flesh and mushroom flesh are also called nyama. Wood is either chiini (heartwood) or bacha (sapwood).

definition.en: The heartwood at the centre of a trunk, found only in trees that grow thick with age. It lasts well and is preferred for carpentry and building.

meaning.en: Purity; Pakia could not explain the link to heartwood.

notes: Mostly used by carpenters, pole cutters and builders, not part of general Digo plant knowledge.

definition.en: The softer outer wood of a trunk. Pests damage it, so it is less wanted for carpentry and building.

notes: Like chiini, a word used mostly by timber users.

definition.en: A branch, or the Y-shaped fork where a stem divides.

meaning.en: Also 'to climb' and a catapult, which is made from a forked branch.

definition.en: A section of stem between two joints, as in sugarcane. The same word names a single cassava tuber.

notes: Finger segments are also pindi; Pakia suggests it is really a counting word. Mgombato gives a sugarcane pindi as about 15 cm.

definition.en: The knob or stump left on a stem when a branch is cut.

meaning.en: Also used for the stump of an amputated hand or leg.

notes: Pakia's table glosses it as 'a bulge on stem'; Mgombato as 'tree stump'.

definition.en: A hollow in a trunk or at a cut branch, as often found in muhuhu (Brachylaena huillensis).

meaning.en: Cave; any hole or hollow.

definition.en: A leaf. Each leaflet of a compound leaf counts as its own kodza. Coloured bracts, seed leaves, spines and tendrils are not counted as kodza.

meaning.en: The Digo describe leaves as the plant's clothing (nguo) against the sun, so a tree losing its leaves 'is changing its clothes' (inabadilisha nguo).

notes: A Mijikenda word; Swahili kept the older Bantu jani. Mgombato also has likodza (makodza). In ceremonies leaves take other names: maruwa, mashada, vwanda.

definition.en: The veins of a leaf.

meaning.en: Veins (of the body).

notes: Mgombato has the singular mshipa: vein, tendon, muscle.

definition.en: The main vein down the middle of a leaf.

meaning.en: 'Backbone of the leaf', from its central position and its likeness to a spine.

notes: Mgombato has mongo: back.

definition.en: The tip of a leaf.

meaning.en: Sharp end; used for any sharp tip.

notes: Pakia recorded no separate word for rounded leaf tips.

definition.en: The stalk of a leaf; the same word is used for the stalk of a fruit or flower.

english: leaf stalk (petiole); fruit or flower stalk
notes: Mgombato glosses mlita as 'stalk of a fruit' and gives mgoti with the same meaning.

definition.en: One lobe of a lobed leaf such as cassava's; the lobes are mala ga kodza, 'fingers of the leaf'. Bananas are counted as mala too.

meaning.en: Finger.

notes: Pakia suggests mala is partly a counting word, from the five lobes of a palm-shaped leaf. A lobed leaf is makodza ga mala, 'leaves with fingers' (§3.3.4).

definition.en: A root. The Digo see roots as the plant's mouth (mromo), through which it eats soil and drinks water.

meaning.en: Mizi also means stability or permanence: 'akachita mizi', 'he has put down roots'.

notes: The fibres in the middle of a cassava tuber are also mizi.

definition.en: A root tuber, as a general word. Most tubers go by their crop's name (manga, cassava; myogwe, sweet potato; nduma, arrowroot), so viazi is used for the Irish potato, which is new and has no name of its own, and for wild tubers.

notes: The Digo class stem tubers such as potatoes with roots, unlike botanists.

definition.en: Small swellings on the roots of legumes and some other plants.

meaning.en: Charm; probably named for looking like a charm. Mgombato: a charm worn on the neck or arm; also handcuffs.

notes: The nodules of ndago sedges are made into a charm for strength in danger.

definition.en: A buttress root, the flat wall-like root at the base of some trees. Pakia says the Digo think these grow on rocky soil, where shallow-rooted trees need extra support against the wind.

notes: Synonyms: ngao ('shield') and mishipa ya mizi, 'neck of the roots' (Pakia also spells it misipha ya mizi), which likens a tree to a person standing on its head.

definition.en: Another word for ngamba, a buttress root.

meaning.en: Shield, for its flat shape and protective role.

definition.en: Small cassava or potato tubers; the only description Pakia found for roots in particular.

meaning.en: Small pieces.

definition.en: A flower. To the Digo a ruwa is a plant part that is colourful or bears fruit: it includes bougainvillea's coloured bracts and the female maize flower, but not the maize tassel.

meaning.en: Carries the idea of beauty: maruwa also means ornamental plants, decorative drawings and hair patterns.

notes: At funerals, maruwa are the leaves packed around the body (§3.3.3). The papaya's male flower is still a ruwa because it looks like the female.

definition.en: A plume-like flower head: the maize tassel, the panicles of grasses such as Guinea grass and sugarcane, and the coconut's florets.

meaning.en: Probably from mphunga, rice.

notes: Mgombato glosses punga as 'flowers of edible green plants like spinach'.

definition.en: A fruit, but only a fleshy one (berry, drupe, citrus and the like). Dry fruits such as maize cobs, groundnuts and bean pods are not tunda.
The skin of a fruit or seed, and the peel of a root tuber.
Wings on winged fruits, as in Gyrocarpus americanus and Combretum schumannii.

meaning.en: Wings.

notes: Pakia could not confirm the term, as these trees were uncommon in some study areas.

definition.en: A seed or kernel; more broadly any grain, as in tembe ya tsere (maize grain) and tembe ya mtsanga (grain of soil).

notes: The older word is mbeyu, but most Digo now prefer tembe. Seeds of plants with no use are called 'tembe ya/za …', e.g. tembe ya manga, tembe za mvure (§3.3.2).

definition.en: Planting material of any kind: seeds, cuttings (vigoda), seedlings (mitse), banana suckers (mwana) and potato eye buds (dzitso). Seeds meant for eating are not mbeyu.

meaning.en: Also used of people for blood lineage.

notes: Pakia also notes it can stand for tunda, fruit.

definition.en: The embryo of a seed, where visible (maize, beans, mango): the part the new plant grows from. Farmers check it before sowing.

notes: Mgombato glosses chitsa as 'kernel of maize or nuts' (Swahili nzima). In the coconut the embryo is called mwezi.

definition.en: The embryo of the coconut, and the cotyledon of the mango seed.

meaning.en: Moon: the coconut embryo is likened to a full moon, the mango cotyledon to a half moon.

definition.en: A scar or bud where new growth comes out: the hilum of a bean, the three 'eyes' on a coconut, the eye buds of a potato.

meaning.en: Eye.

definition.en: A seedling or sapling. Most trees, the coconut among them, are named only in two stages: mutse, then the tree's own name.
Cuttings used to grow new plants.

notes: Pakia gives only the plural.

definition.en: A harmless milky sap, from plants such as Euphorbia hirta (medicinal) and Ficus (used to fix feathers to arrows); also the milky juice of unripe maize grains.

meaning.en: Milk.

definition.en: A caustic, toxic oil from unripe cashew fruits and the shell of mature cashew nuts.
A sticky latex, from Saba comorensis and Landolphia kirkii, used by young people to make sticky bird traps.

notes: Mgombato: gum used to catch birds, made by boiling the resin of certain trees.

definition.en: A sticky resin from cashew bark, used as glue.

meaning.en: From English 'gum'.

definition.en: A burning, itching latex, from Euphorbia nyikae and Synadenium, that harms skin and eyes; some use it as fish poison.

notes: Pakia notes the older Bantu word meant sticky birdlime, the sense now carried by ukaka; Mgombato still glosses ulimbo as resin boiled to make bird gum.

definition.en: A deadly toxic latex from Acokanthera schimperi, used as arrow poison.

meaning.en: Bitterness; also poison.

definition.en: A poultice of crushed leaves used as medicine.

notes: Mgombato vwanda (vwanda1) is a traditional ointment for skin diseases such as ringworm; vwanda2 is chewed sugarcane fibre.

definition.en: A medicinal bath of shredded leaves in a pot of water. Also called vuwo.

meaning.en: Pot.

notes: A technical word known mainly to healers.

definition.en: Leaves worn under the cap by the groom and his party at a wedding. It is an offence to call them makodza on that occasion.

meaning.en: From Arabic shahada, 'declaration'.

definition.en: The part of a plant eaten as a vegetable side dish; for cassava, only the young leaves. Some vegetables have their own names, e.g. mpeya (cassava leaves) and mtsafwe (cowpea leaves).
A fleshy edible mushroom, and in particular its cap, the part eaten. Also called udzondzo.

notes: Also spelled woga (Mgombato's headword). Inedible or non-fleshy ones are woga koma, 'wild mushrooms'. The plural vyoga also names a spotty skin disease.

definition.en: The fleshy, edible part of a mushroom, cap and stem.

meaning.en: 'Mushroom meat', for its flesh and taste.

definition.en: The stem of a mushroom. Also called mgoti.

meaning.en: Stem of the mushroom.

notes: Mgombato's mgoti means 'stalk of a fruit'.

definition.en: The gills under a mushroom cap.

meaning.en: Marks.

notes: Few respondents used it, so Pakia could not confirm it is a genuine Digo term.

definition.en: The young stage of a mushroom while the cap is still closed; this is the stage collectors prefer.
The later stage of a mushroom once the cap has opened; by then it is often infested by small worms.

meaning.en: Mgombato: bumula, to spread out something folded.
